newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse watchdog suspends Co-Nexus broker.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse watchdog suspends Co-Nexus broker.

text.p: Hungary's Securities and Bourse Supervision (AETF) suspended or limited activities of the brokerage Co-Nexus Securities Rt until January 31 and appointed a commissioner to supervise Co-Nexus, AETF said on Wednesday.
AETF said the cause of the measures was that Co-Nexus breached regulations of the Securities Exchange Law and this could also jeopardise the interests of investors.

"(Co-Nexus) announced on November 18 that its CEO had resigned with immediate effect, the board of directors had not appointed a new head, and (Co-Nexus) wanted to cease its securities-trading activities," AETF said.
The restrictions may be lifted before January 31, AETF said in a statement in its official gazette.
The measures forbid Co-Nexus to do securities deals on its own account, to do commission work, and give commissions as asset-manager.
Laszlo Vida, an employee of AETF has been appointed as commissioner to supervise Co-Nexus activities.
Co-Nexus' major shareholder Andras Laszlo said earlier this week that investor confidence in the company collapsed due to political attacks against Co-Nexus.

Co-Nexus Rt, the owner of Co-Nexus Securities, was commissioned to manage state-owned property, for which it will have to pay four billion forints to the State Privatisation Agency APV by the end of this year.
The issue has been raised a number of times in parliament recently, Laszlo said, and this has led to the shaking of investor confidence.
Laszlo said the property placed under Co-Nexus' management was overvalued at the time and was not worth more than half of the four billion forints.
